methodology: Original explanations; GKToday is a discovery/reference source and official treaty, standards and statutory sources are linked.

7103.title: Tropic of Cancer: India's eight states
7103.overview: The Tropic of Cancer lies at about 23°26′ N. It crosses eight Indian states from west to east: Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram.
7103.context: Latitude measures angular distance north or south of the Equator. The Tropic marks the northernmost latitude where the Sun can be overhead at noon, around the June solstice.
7103.who: It crosses eight States; it does not cross Meghalaya, Assam or Nagaland.
7103.what: Earth's axial tilt shifts the Sun's apparent overhead position between the two tropics during the year.
7103.why: The line helps explain India's latitudinal extent and tropical/subtropical geography.
7103.significance: Memory aid west to east: G-R-M-C-J-W-T-M. Do not include Meghalaya or Assam.
7103.exam: GKToday geography reference; original practice explanation.

7104.title: Equator: zero degrees latitude
7104.overview: The Equator is the imaginary great circle at 0° latitude. It divides Earth into Northern and Southern Hemispheres and is the reference from which latitude is measured.
7104.context: Latitude is angular distance north or south of the Equator. Lines of latitude are parallel; the Equator is the largest latitude circle and a great circle.
7104.who: Geographers use it as the zero reference for latitude.
7104.what: A point north has north latitude; a point south has south latitude. It crosses parts of South America, Africa and Asia and several oceans.
7104.why: The coordinate grid needs a consistent baseline for locating places and describing climatic zones.
7104.significance: Do not confuse 0° latitude (Equator) with 0° longitude (Prime Meridian).
7104.exam: GKToday geography question; standard coordinate system.

7107.title: RBI Monetary Policy Committee
7107.overview: The MPC is the statutory rate-setting committee under the RBI Act, 1934. It determines the policy repo rate within India's inflation-targeting framework, with price stability as the primary objective while keeping growth in mind.
7107.context: The Finance Act, 2016 amended the RBI Act to institutionalise committee-based policy decisions. Section 45ZB provides for the MPC.
7107.who: The RBI Governor chairs the six-member committee; three members are from RBI and three external members are appointed by the Central Government.
7107.what: The MPC reviews inflation, growth and liquidity and votes on the policy rate. Decisions are collective; the Governor has a casting vote in a tie.
7107.why: Committee decision-making improves transparency and reduces reliance on a single decision-maker.
7107.significance: Monetary policy affects borrowing costs, credit, demand and inflation; it is distinct from fiscal policy and tax administration.
7107.exam: Legal anchor: RBI Act, 1934, Section 45ZB, as amended by Finance Act 2016. Avoid memorising undated rates.
7107.source: GKToday topic; statutory framework cross-checked with RBI/India Code.

7108.title: GST and the taxable event of supply
7108.overview: GST is an indirect tax whose principal taxable event is supply of goods or services or both. Section 7 of the CGST Act, 2017 defines scope of supply, subject to schedules and exclusions.
7108.context: GST replaced fragmented indirect-tax triggers with a broad supply-based framework.
7108.who: CGST, SGST/UTGST and IGST apply according to the nature and place of supply.
7108.what: Section 7 covers specified forms such as sale, transfer, barter, exchange, licence, rental, lease or disposal when made for consideration in business; Schedule I covers specified supplies without consideration and Schedule III lists activities treated as neither supply.
7108.why: The supply test determines whether a transaction enters the GST charging framework; not every activity is automatically taxable.
7108.significance: For tax-office work, identify supplier, recipient, transaction, consideration, business connection, place of supply and relevant schedule.
7108.exam: Legal anchor: CGST Act Section 7; read with charging provisions and Schedules I–III. Check current amendments.
7108.source: GKToday GST topic; legal framework checked against CBIC.

7109.title: Convention on Biological Diversity, 1992
7109.overview: The CBD is a legally binding treaty adopted at the 1992 Rio Earth Summit. It entered into force on 29 December 1993 and has three core objectives.
7109.context: It emerged from the 1992 UN Conference on Environment and Development.
7109.who: Parties, including India, undertake national action; the Conference of the Parties is the treaty's governing body.
7109.what: Objectives: conservation of biodiversity; sustainable use of its components; fair and equitable sharing of benefits from genetic resources.
7109.why: It links conservation with sustainable use and benefit-sharing, and addresses ecosystem, food-security and livelihood risks.
7109.significance: Memory aid C-S-B: Conservation, Sustainable use, Benefit-sharing. Do not confuse CBD with UNFCCC.
7109.exam: GKToday environment topic; treaty text checked against CBD Secretariat.

7110.title: Ozone layer and the stratosphere
7110.overview: Most atmospheric ozone is in the stratosphere, roughly 10–50 km above Earth. It absorbs much of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet radiation.
7110.context: Ozone is O3; the ozone layer is a region of relatively high concentration, not a solid sheet.
7110.who: Natural sunlight-driven reactions create and destroy ozone; some human-made ozone-depleting substances accelerate its breakdown.
7110.what: About 90% of atmospheric ozone is in the stratosphere. Ground-level ozone in the troposphere is a pollutant and part of photochemical smog.
7110.why: Ozone depletion increases UV exposure; the 1987 Montreal Protocol controls ozone-depleting substances.
7110.significance: Remember: stratospheric ozone protects; tropospheric ozone pollutes. The ozone hole is severe depletion, not a literal hole.
7110.exam: GKToday science/environment reference; atmospheric science checked against NASA.

7111.title: Ampere: SI base unit of electric current
7111.overview: Ampere (A) is the SI base unit of electric current. Current is the rate at which charge passes a point: I = Q/t, so 1 A = 1 coulomb per second.
7111.context: The SI has seven base units; electric current is one base quantity.
7111.who: The unit is named after French physicist André-Marie Ampère.
7111.what: If 10 C pass a point in 2 s, I = 10/2 = 5 A. Voltage is in volts, resistance in ohms and power in watts.
7111.why: The SI provides a consistent way to measure electrical quantities; the modern ampere definition fixes the elementary charge.
7111.significance: Formula I = Q/t; check units: coulomb ÷ second = ampere. Ampere is a base unit; volt, ohm and watt are derived.
7111.exam: GKToday physics reference; SI unit checked against BIPM.

7112.title: Cerebellum: balance, posture and coordination
7112.overview: The cerebellum coordinates movement, maintains posture and balance, and helps make voluntary movements smooth and accurate.
7112.context: It lies at the back of the brain, beneath the occipital lobes and behind the brainstem.
7112.who: It receives information from vestibular organs, spinal cord and cerebral cortex.
7112.what: It adjusts timing and coordination of muscle activity rather than simply initiating voluntary movement.
7112.why: Damage can cause ataxia, poor coordination, unsteady gait and difficulty maintaining posture.
7112.significance: Cerebellum = coordination and balance; cerebrum = higher cognition; medulla = vital involuntary functions.
7112.exam: GKToday human-body question; standard neuroanatomy reference.

7113.title: Kathakali: Kerala's classical dance-drama
7113.overview: Kathakali is a classical dance-drama of Kerala combining dance, music, acting, mime, facial expression and hand gestures.
7113.context: The name is commonly explained as katha (story) and kali (play/performance).
7113.who: Performers enact characters through stylised movement and mudras; vocalists sing while percussion supports the performance.
7113.what: It is a dramatic narrative, not merely abstract dance; makeup and costume signal character types.
7113.why: It preserves regional performance traditions and connects literature, music, theatre and dance.
7113.significance: Compare: Kathakali—Kerala; Kathak—North India; Bharatanatyam—Tamil Nadu; Odissi—Odisha; Kuchipudi—Andhra Pradesh.
7113.exam: GKToday Indian culture topic; state art-form reference checked against Kerala Tourism.

7114.title: CPU: Central Processing Unit
7114.overview: The CPU is the main general-purpose processor. It fetches, decodes and executes program instructions and coordinates processing with memory and input/output devices.
7114.context: A computer system has processing, memory, storage and input/output components; the CPU is not the whole computer.
7114.who: The ALU performs arithmetic and logical operations; the Control Unit directs instruction flow; registers hold small amounts of high-speed working data.
7114.what: The instruction cycle is commonly described as fetch, decode and execute; cache and registers provide fast access to working data.
7114.why: The CPU runs operating-system and application instructions. A GPU is specialised for parallel graphics/compute; RAM is temporary working memory; SSD/HDD stores data persistently.
7114.significance: Distinguish CPU (processing), RAM (temporary memory), SSD/HDD (persistent storage), keyboard/mouse (input) and monitor/printer (output).
7114.exam: GKToday computer-hardware topic; original practice explanation.

7115.title: UN Security Council: primary responsibility
7115.overview: Article 24 of the UN Charter gives the Security Council primary responsibility for international peace and security. It has 15 members: five permanent and ten elected non-permanent members.
7115.context: The Security Council is one of the six principal UN organs; its authority comes from the Charter.
7115.who: Permanent members are China, France, Russia, the UK and the US; the General Assembly elects ten non-permanent members for two-year terms.
7115.what: The Council may investigate disputes, recommend settlement, impose sanctions and authorise measures. Article 25 requires members to carry out its decisions.
7115.why: It is central to the UN collective-security system. A permanent member's negative vote can block a substantive resolution; procedural matters differ.
7115.significance: Article 24 = responsibility; Article 23 = composition; Article 25 = obligation to carry out decisions.
7115.exam: GKToday international-organisation reference; legal basis checked against UN Charter.

7116.title: The Guide (1958) by R. K. Narayan
7116.overview: The Guide is a 1958 novel by R. K. Narayan, set in fictional Malgudi. It follows Raju, whose life changes from railway guide to a man regarded by villagers as a spiritual guide.
7116.context: Narayan used Malgudi to explore ordinary lives, social change and moral ambiguity.
7116.who: R. K. Narayan is the author; Raju is the central character; Rosie and Marco are important to the plot.
7116.what: Raju becomes involved in Rosie's life and career, is imprisoned after a fraud, and later lives in a village where his fasting is interpreted as spiritual.
7116.why: The novel is important in modern Indian English literature for its Indian setting, accessible prose and complex character development.
7116.significance: Do not confuse The Guide with Untouchable (Mulk Raj Anand), Kanthapura (Raja Rao) or Train to Pakistan (Khushwant Singh).
7116.exam: GKToday books-and-authors topic; author context checked against standard literary references.
